title: rollout-accordion-sprint-matrix-and-telemetry-snackpad-mar-2028-sketch
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, informal pocket plan for the March accordion sprint release. Focus is on: fast incremental traffic moves, regional sequencing (US-EAST -> EU -> APAC), compact telemetry checks (1/5/15m), and an abbreviated rollback ladder that can be executed by on-call without engineering deep-dive.

High-level objectives:
- Ship v2 batch-routing (small config change, opt-in via header).
- Validate new batching affinity in production without impacting 99.9 latency SLOs.
- Keep cost impact < +4% token cost for the first 24h.

Scope (what's in):
- Router config + canary gate (header-based pin).
- Two compatible model variants (v2-perf, v2-safe) already baked in images.
- Observability dashboards (latency, p50/p90/p99, error rate, model CPU/GPU tail).

Out-of-scope:
- Schema changes to client API.
- Large-scale DB migrations.

Quiet windows / blackout:
- Avoid doing final cutover during 2028-03-18 17:00-21:00 PT (end-of-week support overlap).
- Maintenance window earlier same week (Mon 03/12) used for canary infra warm-ups.

Rollout rhythm (accordion pattern):
Phase A — micro-canary (hosted traffic, 0.5%): 30m observation
Phase B — micro-burst (hosted 2.5%): 45m observation
Phase C — regional stretch (US-EAST 10% -> EU 10% -> APAC 5%): 60m per region
Phase D — ramp to baseline (each region incremental steps to 50% over 4 hrs)

Hour-by-hour quick calendar (local times shown as PT):
- T-24: Run smoke job, confirm perf baselines, notify CS + SRE slack channel #launch
- T-2: Freeze non-critical deploys, finalize comms, on-call assigned
- T+0: Start Phase A (0.5%) — note exact time in release thread
- T+0.5h: Check telemetry snapshot (see thresholds below)
- T+1.5h: Move to Phase B if green
- T+3h: Begin Phase C (regional) — US-EAST -> EU -> APAC sequentially
- T+8h: Post-roll notes draft and initial usage/cost check

Telemetry quick-check (snackpad):
Primary signals (1/5/15m windows):
- request.latency.p99: baseline + 40ms allowed for micro-canary, +100ms for regional ramp
- error.rate (5xx): absolute < 0.2% for all traffic shards
- model.kv-cache-hit: should be >= baseline - 2% (if drops, abort)
- GPU-utilization tail: no single node > 95% sustained for 5m
- downstream queue length: no queue increase > 3x baseline for 1m

Automated gates (what auto-blocks):
- p99 > baseline + 150ms for more than 3 consecutive 1m buckets -> auto-fallback to v1 route
- 5xx > 0.5% sustained 5m -> abort and rollback to previous routing

Manual gates (require two eyes + on-call signoff):
- model.ioErrors increase 0.2% -> needs eng triage and canary pause
- cost delta > +6% over rolling 30m -> product + finance consult

Smoke checklist (pre-flight):
- [ ] Canary harness deployed in staging and smoke tests passing (smoke id: smoke-03-12)
- [ ] Canary manifests versioned & PR merged: PR #2124
- [ ] Run synthetic embedding job and compare p95 against baseline (script: tools/sim-embed.sh)
- [ ] Confirm dashboards replicate across regions (link pasted in thread)
- [ ] Confirm alert escalation matrix (SRE pager, product lead, release owner)
- [ ] Backup route config and create restore patch (doc link in linked_artifacts)

Rollback ladder (fast):
- Step 1: Flip routing header to keep v1 default (config flag: routing.fallback = true)
- Step 2: If Step 1 insufficient, scale v2 down by 60% via autoscale-policy quickset
- Step 3: Revert full config via hot patch and run post-rollback smoke (10m)
- Step 4: Create incident ticket and assign severity (if > 30m impact).

Communication plan (who/where):
- Live release thread: #release-ops (Slack) — primary comms
- Pager escalation: SRE -> Eng on-call -> Release owner (Aisha)
- Customer comms: CS standby, draft update template in /cs/templates/rollout-brief.md

Post-release checks (T+1h, T+8h, T+24h):
- Quick sanity (T+1h): confirm p99, errors, cost delta (<4%)
- Health digest (T+8h): short report, key metrics and anomalies, attach minimal changelog
- Full review (T+24h): determine if variant effects on quality observed; decide on full ramp or rollback

Release notes (draft snippets):
- feature: v2 batch-routing - improves throughput for high-concurrent chat scenarios; opt-in via header
- perf: ~8-12% CPU efficiency gain on warm KV cache paths (expected lower cost per token)
- compatibility: model contract unchanged — clients not using header see no change
- known issues: potential transient p99 bump on cold-start in APAC; watch telemetry

Open questions / ToDos:
- Q: Do we want a controlled experiment for embeddings vs. generation paths? (ask research)
- TODO: Add metrics sampling to reduce noise when traffic low (Evan)
- TODO: Finalize cost alert thresholds with finance (Priya)

Retrospective anchors (postmortem template pointers):
- Timeline (T-24 -> T+24) with screenshots of dashboards
- Decisions log (who greenlit each phase)
- Root cause if rollback (include system traces and model traces)

Notes to self / scratch: 
- Keep the regional ramp small and sequential; the whole point of accordion is to deflate sudden cluster pressure.
- If we see model.kv-cache-hit drop in EU, consider delaying APAC by +2h.
- Write a tiny script to snapshot the config and upload to s3 before each phase (small ops automation win).

Appendix (quick links & commands):
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2124
- Canary smoke: ./tools/sim-embed.sh --profile release-03-12
- Restore command (kubectl patch): kubectl patch configmap routing -p '{\"data\":{\"fallback\":\"true\"}}'

-- end of sketch --
